responses.response: Keep this in deployment-focused guidance. The shared deployment spec already defines Dmz, AppTier, ProcTier, and DataTier as tier tags, so splitting production that way is in scope. Model each tier as a Zone with the matching tag, place Infra_Fw where the boundary matters, and add only the allowed cross-zone infrastructure links. You only need different guidance if the problem stops being about deployment structure and boundaries.

Usually no. The shared cheat sheet says to put interaction technology on the system-model relationship, and to add a port only when it is non-default for the protocol. It also says deployment relationships are for infrastructure-specific connections, while normal application traffic should usually be inherited in deployment through instanceOf. So webApp -> apiApp and apiApp -> dbApp should normally live in the logical model, using the relationship type that matches the behavior there. For the database side, prefer the logical relationship that expresses the behavior, such as reads or writes, and attach the technology there. Keep deployment.c4 for deployment-only edges like firewall hops, monitoring scrapes, backup mounts, or other infrastructure links.

Add the Prometheus scrape as a deployment relationship, because it is infrastructure or observability traffic rather than duplicated business traffic. Model Prometheus as a deployment node and connect it with http or https to the real scrape target: Prometheus -> apiVm if it scrapes VM-level metrics, or Prometheus -> apiApp if it scrapes the application metrics endpoint. Avoid re-adding browser -> API traffic that already exists in the logical model, and avoid duplicating other normal application flows that instanceOf already brings into deployment.
